learningObjective: Reason about FP16-in/FP32-accumulate GEMM: numerics and Tensor Core hardware path.

canonicalClaims.claim: FP16-input GEMM commonly uses FP32 accumulation to preserve precision across long K-dimension reductions; on sm_70+ Tensor Cores natively support this mixed-precision mode via `mma.sync` with FP16 operands and FP32 accumulator.
conditions: Triton lowers `tl.dot(out_dtype=fp32)` to mma.sync when possible.
nonImplications: Does not imply FP32 accumulation is exact.
Does not imply short reductions require FP32 accum.

misconceptions.claim: FP32-accumulate + downcast is bit-identical to full-FP16 pipeline.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Intermediate precision changes the result of long sums.

misconceptions.claim: CUDA `mma.sync`/`wmma` cannot mix input and accumulator precisions.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Mixed precision (FP16 in, FP32 accum) is a Tensor Core selling point.

misconceptions.claim: Long FP16 accumulations are safe because 16-bit precision is sufficient for most models.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Rounding error accumulates quadratically-in-magnitude with reduction length.

misconceptions.claim: FP32 accumulation halves Tensor Core throughput vs FP16 accumulation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: On many architectures FP32-accum is at the same rate as FP16-accum (they use the same MMA); on some, FP16-accum is faster. Architecture-specific check required.

implementationFacts: Triton lowers `tl.dot(a, b, out_dtype=tl.float32)` with FP16 inputs to mma.sync.
